## Item 17 — Login rate limiting / lockout (carried from v1.6.5)

- **Status:** ✅ **DONE `df83f3f`** (2026-07-14, on-device verified by Alvin). **Model: Sonnet, low** (built on Opus this session — pure state-machine mirror of the PIN lockout, no open design calls). Non-paywall, internal-only. Carried over from [v1.6.5.md](v1.6.5.md) Item 17 (decision settled 2026-07-14). No schema/Room change (stays **v25**).
- **Decision recap:** the GoTrue password-sign-in endpoint is governed by the per-IP "token refreshes" limit (~150/5min), not a per-account cap, and can't be tightened safely (PH carrier-grade NAT shares IPs). So the control is a **per-device client cooldown** — deterrence + parity with the PIN lock, explicitly **not** true brute-force protection (a real attacker hits the API directly).
- **As built:** new pure `feature/auth/domain/model/LoginLockoutPolicy` (mirrors `PinLockoutPolicy`) — `MAX_ATTEMPTS = 5`, `COOLDOWN_SECONDS = 30`, `onFailure(count)` returning the next count + lockout seconds, resetting the counter to 0 when it locks so lockouts recur in clean 5-strike cycles. `AuthUiState` gained `failedSignInAttempts` + `signInLockoutSeconds` and `canSubmit` now requires `signInLockoutSeconds == 0`. `AuthViewModel.submit` counts **only** an `INVALID_CREDENTIALS` sign-in failure (never a network/rate-limit error, never sign-up), applies the policy, and on lockout starts a `lockoutClearJob` that re-enables after the cooldown (mirrors `AppLockViewModel`); a successful sign-in cancels it and clears the count. `AuthScreen` shows "Too many attempts. Try again in Xs." under the disabled button. Pure client state machine — no repo/sync/schema touch.
- **Files touched:** new `feature/auth/domain/model/LoginLockoutPolicy.kt`, `feature/auth/presentation/{AuthUiState, AuthViewModel, AuthScreen}.kt`.
- **Tests:** +4 tier-1 JVM (`LoginLockoutPolicyTest` — early failure increments, sub-threshold no-lock, threshold locks + resets, full-cycle locks exactly once). `testStagingDebugUnitTest` (910 total, 0 failures) + `assembleStagingDebug` green.

## Item 25 — Privacy mode defaults ON per session (auto-hide per session, carried from v1.6.5)

- **Status:** ✅ **DONE** — `8ec1339` (`AppLockManager` + `MainActivity`, landed inside the widget commit) + **`8e87d37`** (`PrivacyModeRepositoryImpl`) (2026-07-14, on-device verified by Alvin). **Model: Sonnet, low–medium** (built on Opus this session — flag + lifecycle wiring, no novel design). Non-paywall (privacy). Carried over from [v1.6.5.md](v1.6.5.md) Item 25 (decision settled 2026-07-14, option b). No schema/Room change (stays **v25**).
- **Decision recap (option b):** default ON (fresh/cold open → amounts hidden); a reveal is per-session, non-persisted; re-hides after inactivity tied to the **same ~30s app-lock grace** (a quick <grace bounce keeps the reveal; a background past grace re-hides). No new timer — rides `AppLockManager`'s existing lifecycle boundary.
- **As built:** `PrivacyModeRepositoryImpl` dropped DataStore for an in-memory `MutableStateFlow` seeded **hidden** (`true`), so a cold process starts masked. The re-hide rides a new `AppLockManager.autoLockElapsed: SharedFlow<Unit>` — emitted when the grace timer completes, **PIN-independent** (unlike `isLocked`, which dedups and never cycles for a no-PIN user, so it couldn't drive this). The repo collects `autoLockElapsed` → set hidden. `MainActivity`'s `LocalPrivacyMode` initial value → `true` so the first frame is masked. The `PrivacyModeRepository` interface + `Observe`/`SetPrivacyModeUseCase` are **unchanged**, so the three Item-15 reveal entry points (Settings switch, Accounts/Analysis eye icons) and the in-flight balance-widget consumer are undisturbed — they now flip the session flag instead of a persisted value. The `privacy_prefs` DataStore provider is left in DI (unused, harmless — no persisted-schema change per the decision).
- **Files touched:** `feature/applock/presentation/AppLockManager.kt` (+`autoLockElapsed`, in `8ec1339`), `MainActivity.kt` (initial=true, in `8ec1339`), `feature/settings/data/PrivacyModeRepositoryImpl.kt` (in `8e87d37`).
- **Note (commit split):** because the in-flight widget work had already refactored `AppLockManager` (adding `setLocked`) and `MainActivity` in the working tree, Item 25's edits to those two files rode the widget commit `8ec1339`; the standalone `PrivacyModeRepositoryImpl` conversion is `8e87d37`. Functionally one slice, split across two commits by working-tree entanglement.
- **Tests:** none added — pure flag + lifecycle wiring (verify-by-running per Testing Policy; no pure predicate to extract). `testStagingDebugUnitTest` (910, 0 failures) + `assembleStagingDebug` green. On-device verified by Alvin.

## Item 23 — Archived entity label fallback in Records & Budgets (⏸️ DEFERRED — needs tester feedback)

- **Status:** ⏸️ **DEFERRED** — moved here from [v1.6.5.md](v1.6.5.md) Item 23 (2026-07-14). Booked but intentionally **not scheduled**; Alvin wants **tester feedback first** before deciding whether it's a bug to fix or the intended signal. Split out of [v1.6.5.md Item 19](v1.6.5.md) to keep that slice tightly scoped. **Model (if built): Sonnet, low effort.** Non-paywall.
- **Independent** — pure display-time label resolution, no schema/sync/data change.

**Surfaced 2026-07-11** while confirming Item 19's archive semantics. Records and Budgets resolve a category/account **name from its id** via a lookup map built from `observeCategories()` / `observeAccounts()` at the default `includeArchived = false`. So a **historical row pointing at a now-archived entity** drops out of the map and falls back to a generic label:
- **Records list** ([TransactionsViewModel.toListItem](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/transactions/presentation/TransactionsViewModel.kt#L161)) — a transaction whose **category** was archived reads **"Uncategorized"** (`categoryNames[categoryId] ?: "Uncategorized"`); whose **account** was archived reads **"Account"** (`accountNames[accountId] ?: "Account"`).
- **Budgets** ([BudgetsViewModel](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/budgets/presentation/BudgetsViewModel.kt#L78)) — an existing budget on a now-archived category reads **"Category"** (`categoryNames[it] ?: "Category"`); the budget still tracks spending correctly, only the name degrades.

**The inconsistency:** [Analysis](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/analysis/presentation/AnalysisViewModel.kt#L83) deliberately observes `includeArchived = true` so archived categories **keep their label** in the donut/flow; Recurring materialization does the same. Records and Budgets never got that treatment, so the **same archived category is labeled three different ways** depending on the screen. It is **purely cosmetic** — no data loss (the row still carries its `categoryId`/`accountId`), and **unarchiving restores every label instantly** (the entity re-enters the map).

**The product question to answer with tester feedback (why it's deferred, not just built):** is an archived category *supposed* to keep naming its old transactions in Records (consistent with Analysis), or is **"Uncategorized"** the intended cue that "this category is retired"? Don't change the behavior until this is decided.

**If built (the shape):** Records is a one-line switch to `observeCategories(includeArchived = true)` / `observeAccounts(includeArchived = true)` (it uses the list only for label lookup, not a picker). Budgets is a **two-line split** — build the label map from an archived-inclusive observe, but keep the **new-budget picker** (`expenseCategories = categories.filter { it.type == EXPENSE }`) filtered to **active** categories so archived ones don't reappear as budgetable options. (The Add-Transaction / Quick-add / Recurring-editor pickers stay `false` — archived items must not be offered for *new* activity.)

**Verify (if built):** archive a category with existing transactions + a budget → Records rows keep the real name (not "Uncategorized"), the budget row keeps its name (not "Category"), Analysis unchanged; the archived category does **not** appear in the Add-Transaction picker or the new-budget picker; unarchive → everything unchanged.
